players.product: silicon-photonics foundry services (PH18 SiPho platform) + SiGe drivers/TIAs

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 AND FULL-YEAR 2025 RESULTS (CEO/CFO): Q4 revenue $440 million, a record, up 11% quarter-over-quarter and 14% year-over-year, meeting the start-of-year target of sequential growth every quarter. Q4 gross profit $118 million (+26% QoQ), operating profit $71 million (+40% QoQ), net profit $80 million = 18% net margin (up from 11% in Q1, 13% in Q2 and 14% in Q3 2025), diluted EPS $0.70. Q4 net profit includes a nonrecurring tax benefit (all-in 2% effective rate; CFO put the gap at about $10 million); from 2026, Pillar 2 means an all-in tax rate of at least 15% at all manufacturing sites. CEO: revenue grew $82 million from Q1 to Q4 2025, of which $40 million dropped to net profit (48.78%), because the incremental photonics revenue is high value. Full-year 2025 revenue $1.566 billion (+$130 million, a 9% increase), gross profit $364 million, operating profit $194 million, net profit $220 million ($1.94 diluted EPS). A $105 million upfront prepayment in Q4 extended the Newport Beach (Fab 3) lease by 3.5 years, to the end of 2030 (it was due to end in early 2027).
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $440 million (11% quarter-over-quarter, 14% year-over-year); net profit $80 million or 18% net margin; full-year revenue $1.566 billion (9% increase)

quarterly_data.signal: SIPHO / SIGE DRIVE THE MIX, AND THE NVIDIA PARTNERSHIP: RF infrastructure revenue rose 75% in 2025, the fastest-growing application, 'driven by hyperscaler rapid adoption of silicon photonics in 800G and 1.6T pluggable transceivers', and was 32% of Q4 corporate revenue. SiGe plus SiPho = $421 million, or 27% of 2025 revenue (vs $241 million / 17% in 2024). SiPho alone went from $106 million (2024) to $228 million (2025). Q4 SiPho was $95 million, a $380 million annual run rate, which includes some non-wafer NRE for Gen+1 and Gen+2 development. CEO on the recently announced NVIDIA partnership: 'the insatiable demand for compute bandwidth in both scale-up and scale-out architectures' has made '1.6 terabyte per second, the fastest-growing silicon photonics node in the industry to date, with Tower being by far the majority supplier of 1.6T silicon PICs'. Asked by analysts, he said Tower does NOT ship photonics directly to NVIDIA; its silicon photonics ICs 'are all being designed by and shipped through other module makers or integrators'. The partnership covers 'alignments and needs directly and through our module customers and understandings of supply needs and commitments on supply shipments'. In 2025, SiPho production ramped at Fab 9 San Antonio and Fab 7 Uozu (Japan), in addition to Fab 3 Newport Beach. Fab 2 Migdal Haemek is on track to ship the first production of a very large SiPho ramp in 2026. SiGe grew 43% in 2025 and remains the 'optimal platform solution for low-power, low-latency, high-performance components' (drivers and TIAs for pluggables, LPOs, and active copper and active optical cables). SiGe runs in high volume at Fab 3, Fab 9 and Fab 2, and 300mm SiGe prototypes have shipped from Fab 7.
quarterly_data.figure: SiPho revenues $228 million in 2025, up from $106 million in 2024; Q4 SiPho $95 million or a $380 million annual run rate; SiGe + SiPho $421 million (27%); silicon germanium growth of 43%

quarterly_data.signal: SIPHO CAPACITY PLAN RAISED FROM 3X TO MORE THAN 5X: the November 2025 plan targeted tripling SiPho capacity vs Q4-2025 SiPho shipments, online for silicon starts in H2 2026. 'Due to continued growth in demand', Tower added $270 million of equipment CapEx on top of the $650 million already announced, for a $920 million total. The money goes to the 8-inch fabs in Israel, Newport Beach and Texas and the 12-inch Uozu fab in Japan, and a large part is capability CapEx for advanced development and high-end RF. The target is now capacity greater than 5x the Q4-2025 monthly SiPho wafer shipments. CEO: in Q4 2026 Tower plans 5x the silicon wafer capacity it shipped in Q4 2025. Over 70% of total SiPho capacity is reserved or being reserved through 2028, 'firmly backed with customer prepayment'. Multiple customers asked for capacity reservation agreements through 2028 so they can give firm commitments to their own customers; CEO: 'we did not ask customers for reservation fees, they wanted it'. About 28% of the $920 million had been paid; the other 72% is due in 2026 and 2027. Timing: some tools have already arrived, and the bulk arrives by mid-third quarter 2026. The biggest portion should be qualified on or before Q3, and the target is everything fully qualified for customer starts by December 2026. The CEO said 1-3 tools could slip to January or February, but 'the demand is there, it's committed, and it will be used'.
quarterly_data.figure: additional CapEx investment of $270 million on top of the previously announced $650 million ($920 million total); capacity growth greater than 5x; over 70% of the total SiPho capacity reserved through 2028; 28% paid

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FAB UTILIZATION, THE INTEL FAB 11X DISPUTE, AND FUNGIBILITY: Fab 2 ran at about 60% (final stages of SiGe/SiPho capacity qualification). Fab 3 held the model's full utilization of 85% while still adding SiPho capacity. Fab 5 ran at 75%, Fab 7 was fully utilized (well above the 85% model), and Fab 9 ran at 65% (in the SiPho/SiGe ramp). CEO: Intel 'has expressed its intention not to perform under the September '23 Fab 11X agreement'; the two companies are in mediation. All flows moved or being moved to Fab 11X were first qualified in Tower's 300mm Fab 7 in Japan, and 'Customers are being redirected to be supported by this fab in Japan'. Fab 11X is excluded from the new model. On capacity: SiPho alone would not bring the fabs to 85% utilization, but RF SOI capacity is fairly fungible to power and imaging, and SiPho is 'very fungible to silicon germanium'.
quarterly_data.figure: Fab 2 about 60%, Fab 3 85%, Fab 5 75%, Fab 7 fully utilized, Fab 9 65%

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 GUIDANCE (CEO): midrange revenue of $412 million ±5%, a 15% increase over the start of 2025. Tower targets quarter-over-quarter growth in both revenue and profitability throughout 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 midrange revenue $412 million plus/minus 5%, a 15% increase

quarterly_data.signal: UPDATED TARGET FINANCIAL MODEL (presented on this call, replacing the prior model from more than 2 years ago; a point-in-time target): $2.84 billion revenue, 39.4% gross margin, 31.7% operating margin and $750 million net profit (26.4% net margin), which the company targets to reach in calendar year 2028. CEO: certainly on a run-rate basis, possibly for the full year. Assumptions: no CapEx beyond the $920 million plan, Tower-owned capacity at 85% utilization, Intel Fab 11X excluded, modest ASP erosion on existing flows offset by new flows, and all tools and customer qualifications done within 2026. CFO: revenue is $1.27 billion (81%) above FY2025. The model has $1.12 billion gross profit (about 40%, 59% incremental), $900 million operating profit (4.6x FY2025, 32%, 55% incremental) and 42% incremental net margin. Gross, operating and net profit are 50%-60% higher than in the prior model from more than 2 years ago, mostly from the higher SiPho and SiGe mix. CEO: this is a 3-year revenue CAGR of 22% and a net profit CAGR of 50.5%. Customers have committed the demand, and execution is 'really in our hands' along with the suppliers'.
quarterly_data.figure: $2.84 billion revenue; 39.4% gross margin; 31.7% operating margin; $750 million net profit (26.4%); target calendar year 2028; revenue CAGR of 22%, net profit CAGR of 50.5%

quarterly_data.signal: NEXT GENERATION: 400G PER LANE, 3.2T AND CPO (CEO): for 400-gigabit per lane, Tower reports strong progress with heterogeneously integrated indium phosphide on silicon and other material systems. It is working with lead customers to choose the material systems and refine the flow, to ensure 'immediate ramp capability upon 3.2T market introduction'. Co-packaged optics is 'a substantially incremental opportunity for us in the coming years, as optics gets adopted and scale-up interconnects as well as XPU to high-bandwidth memory interconnects that are today largely copper'. In Q4-2025, Tower expanded its mature 300 millimeter wafer bonding to wafer-to-wafer integration of SiPho ICs with SiGe electrical ICs. It is also working with several customers on DWDM laser sources, 'a critical component of many CPO implementations', which would extend its served optical market to the laser source. There is no direct packaging of the CPU, but 'we're certainly working with XPU makers on CPO strategies'. Outside transceivers, the SiPho platform is the choice for FMCW LIDAR in physical AI; partners AVA and LightIC announced collaborations with Tower ahead of CES.
quarterly_data.figure: 400-gigabit per lane / 3.2T readiness; 300 millimeter wafer bonding for SiPho-SiGe wafer-to-wafer integration

quarterly_data.signal: NON-OPTICAL PLATFORMS AND 800V DC (CEO): RF mobile was 23% of 2025 revenue and 24% of Q4. It fell 15% year over year as Tower deliberately cut lower-margin controller products and front-end modules shifted from 200mm to 300mm. 300mm RFSOI grew 5.5%, and Tower won 3 of the top 4 Tier 1 RF front-end module providers: one is already in production, with a strong ramp in 2027 and appreciable volumes in 2028. Power management grew 20% (16% of 2025 revenue), helped by the 300mm ramp of a Tier 1 handset envelope tracker. Asked about 800-volt DC for next-generation AI server racks: 'We don't, at this moment, have an 800-volt platform on an IC. We do have 800-volt capabilities in Fabs, but not in an IC.' Tower does have higher-voltage IC capabilities with and without SOI. Sensors and displays grew 10% on machine vision, and the first AR-display OLED-on-silicon backplane entered production. Mixed-signal CMOS (7%) fell 18% and discretes (11%) fell 14%, which frees capacity for higher-margin platforms. On the memory shortage and handset volumes: the CEO sees some risk, but that capacity is fungible and could be backfilled with lower-margin products.
quarterly_data.figure: RF mobile as a whole was down 15%; 300mm RFSOI was up 5.5%; Power Management grew 20%; 3 of the top 4 Tier 1 RF front-end module providers
